source.title: HoneyBee: Data Recipes for Vision-Language Reasoners
source.authors: Hritik Bansal; D. Sachan; Kai-Wei Chang; Aditya Grover; Gargi Ghosh; Wen-Tau Yih; Ramakanth Pasunuru

record.file_problem: none; full paper and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: Extends downstream scaling findings to vision-language reasoners trained by supervised fine-tuning, measuring accuracy as training-data dimensions and dataset size increase. It does not reproduce the original pretraining-loss measurements.
record.gate_note: The study reports downstream accuracy trends from data-scaling sweeps, which bear on V6. It does not measure held-out cross-entropy loss, fit power laws to loss, test compute-optimal parameter/token allocations, or compare architecture shapes. Other results about dataset curation and model comparisons are not scaling-law measurements.
record.test_reason: The study varies supervised fine-tuning data scale for vision-language reasoners (images, questions per image, CoTs per pair, and HoneyBee subsets from 50K to 2.5M). It reports average downstream accuracy at each scale for PLM 1B, 3B and 8B. This bears weakly on V6 in a new setting: fine-tuning data rather than pretraining scale. No power law or other functional form is fitted and nothing is extrapolated, so only the 'improves with scale' part is tested, not 'predictably'. It never measures loss, so V1–V5 and V7 are not tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that VL reasoning accuracy improves when scaling images, questions per image and CoTs per pair. They also conclude that HoneyBee-trained PLMs (1B–8B) keep improving up to 2.5M examples without saturation. No functional scaling law is fitted.
record.recipe_differences: The original studies measure language-model pretraining loss across parameter, token, or compute scales; HoneyBee varies supervised fine-tuning reasoning-data scale and measures downstream accuracy in vision-language tasks.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported accuracy trend is examined across data axes (images, questions, and CoTs), model sizes (3B and 8B), and HoneyBee dataset sizes; no fitting-method sensitivity is tested.

fits_no_version.finding: Across all data-curation experiments, PLM-3B and PLM-8B average accuracies correlate strongly (r=0.96 on the average; r=0.57 on MathVision). This suggests data decisions made with small models transfer to larger ones.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Rankings of data-curation choices made on small models predict rankings on larger models.

record.peer_reviewed: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (venue stated in metadata); the text identifies the paper as a report.
record.problems: The relevant scaling outcomes are plotted without numerical values or uncertainty estimates in the supplied text. The study measures downstream accuracy after supervised fine-tuning, not held-out pretraining loss, and does not fit or test power-law forms.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows for unrelated curation interventions, model comparisons, RL results, or test-time decoding; they do not measure a scaling-law version in the claim.

untested.parts: All of it: no held-out loss is measured against parameters, tokens or compute.
All of it: no fit, no extrapolation.
All of it: no compute-optimal allocation.
All of it: no shape comparison.
Power-law form in fine-tuning or vision-language training. Accuracy trends are shown but no functional form is fitted.
Predictability (no fitted trend or forecast), dependence on pretraining loss, and pretraining-scale effects. Only monotone improvement with fine-tuning data size over 8x–50x ranges is shown.
All of it: no fitting choices are compared.

missing.what: Per-benchmark scaling curves for HoneyBee subsets across ten evaluation sets. These would show whether improvement is uniform or uneven per task.
Downstream accuracy against model size (1B, 3B, 8B) after identical HoneyBee SFT. The average rises with parameter count.
A claim that the dataset was scaled to 5M VL instances 'with consistent improvements'. No figure or number backs it in the text.

record.verdict_notes: This is a weak test of V6. 'Scale' here means supervised fine-tuning data size, not pretraining scale. The sweeps span only one to two orders of magnitude, and the trends are shown only in figures, with no numbers or uncertainty. HoneyBee subsets also change composition (VL plus text-only) as they grow, which confounds pure size. The study is not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens, or compute, including power-law behavior over several orders of magnitude.
Extrapolating held-out loss from small runs to much larger runs.
Compute-optimal allocation between parameters and training tokens, and its trend with compute.
Effects of depth, width, or other architecture choices at fixed parameter count.
Whether the same power-law form holds across modalities or training regimes; the study measures downstream accuracy in vision-language fine-tuning, not power-law loss.
The study tests downstream accuracy as training-data scale changes, but not downstream performance as a function of pretraining loss or parameter-count scaling.
Dependence of fitted loss exponents or compute-optimal allocations on setup and fitting choices, and bending of loss curves away from a power law.

relationships.condition: SFT data scaling of PLM 1B/3B/8B on VL reasoning: images, questions and CoTs each over an 8x range; HoneyBee 50K→2.5M
relationships.reason: Average downstream VL accuracy rises along every data axis and model size, and is not saturated at 2.5M (R1–R12). Figure only; no fitted law.
relationships.display_finding: Average visual reasoning accuracy increased along every data axis and with model size, without saturating at 2.5M examples.
